Cavort

/kuh-VORT/ - rhymes with resort · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Cavort means to leap about, behave boisterously.

The spring lambs cavorted across the pasture, springing sideways at nothing at all.

Worked Example

Between floats, the costumed mascots cavorted down the parade route — leapfrogging traffic cones, spinning surprised bystanders, high-kicking through the marching band's gaps.

Cavort is bigger than play and bouncier than dance: it is whole-body, look-at-me friskiness — leaping, tumbling, wheeling about. Animals cavort in fields; children cavort in leaf piles; adults cavort mostly at weddings, and deny it on Monday.

How Cavort Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

frolic

frolic: lighter and sweeter — play without the showing off

gambol

gambol: to skip and leap playfully, said mostly of lambs and children

Antonyms

trudge

trudge: to walk heavily, joy nowhere in sight

plod

plod: to move slowly and dully onward

How Strong Is It? — skip → romp → cavort

skip vs. cavort

skip vs. cavort: A skip is one happy bounce in a walk — the smallest, tamest cousin of a cavort.

romp vs. cavort

romp vs. cavort: A romp is energetic, but cavorting is wilder still — add the leaping, the wheeling, and the pleasure in being watched.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — cavort

Root — cavort: origin uncertain — perhaps from curvet, a horse's playful half-leap

Put it together

Put it together: There is nothing to peel off here: cavort appeared in American English around 1800, origin uncertain — the best guess ties it to curvet, a riding-school term for a horse's playful half-leap. However it was born, the word has meant the same thing ever since: joyful, showy leaping about.

Why there's no relative to spot

Why there's no relative to spot: Because cavort's own parentage is a guess, it built no word family — no prefix, no shared root. If the curvet theory is right, its only relative is that rare riding term, which most dictionaries now file under 'horses, historical.'

Strength Check

Word Choice

informal / playful

Cavort when the joy is physical and a little showy — bodies in motion, dignity optional. Frolic is gentler, romp is loose energetic play, and this unit's carouse is the tablebound cousin: carousers sing and pour; cavorters leap and spin.
